verses.gurmukhi: ਦੁਹੁ ਮਿਲਿ ਜੰਮੇ ਦੁਇ ਜਣੇ ਦੁਹੁ ਜਣਿਆਂ ਦੁਇ ਰਾਹ ਚਲਾਏ।
verses.translit_en: dhuh mil ja(n)me dhui jane dhuh janiaa(n) dhui raeh chalaae|

en.bdb: Consequent to the confluence of male and female both (Hindu and Muslim) were born; but both initiated separate ways (sects).

verses.gurmukhi: ਹਿੰਦੂ ਆਖਨਿ ਰਾਮ ਰਾਮ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਣਾਂ ਨਾਉ ਖੁਦਾਏ।
verses.translit_en: hi(n)dhoo aakhan raam raam musalamaanaa(n) naau khudhaae|

en.bdb: Hindus remember Ram-Ram and the Muslims named Him Khuda.

verses.gurmukhi: ਹਿੰਦੂ ਪੂਰਬਿ ਸਉਹਿਆਂ ਪਛਮਿ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਣ ਨਿਵਾਏ।
verses.translit_en: hi(n)dhoo poorab sauhiaa(n) pachham musalamaan nivaae|

en.bdb: Hindus perform their worship facing East and Muslims bow towards the West.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੰਗ ਬਨਾਰਸਿ ਹਿੰਦੂਆਂ ਮਕਾ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਣੁ ਮਨਾਏ।
verses.translit_en: ga(n)g banaaras hi(n)dhooaa(n) makaa musalamaan manaae|

en.bdb: Hindus adore Ganges and Banaras, whereas Muslims celebrate Mecca.

verses.gurmukhi: ਵੇਦ ਕਤੇਬਾ ਚਾਰਿ ਚਾਰਿ ਚਾਰ ਵਰਨ ਚਾਰਿ ਮਜਹਬ ਚਲਾਏ।
verses.translit_en: vedh katebaa chaar chaar chaar varan chaar majahab chalaae|

en.bdb: They have four scriptures each--four Vedas and four Katebas. Hindus created four varnas (castes) and Muslims the four sects (Hanifis, Safis, Malikis, and Hambalis).

verses.gurmukhi: ਪੰਜ ਤਤ ਦੋਵੈ ਜਣੇ ਪਉਣੁ ਪਾਣੀ ਬੈਸੰਤਰੁ ਛਾਏ।
verses.translit_en: pa(n)j tat dhovai jane paun paanee baisa(n)tar chhaae|

en.bdb: But in fact, the same air, water and fire exist in them all.
The ultimate shelter for both is the same one; only they have given different names to it.
